function: Maps carrier-frequency uplink pilot measurements to TTD delays and phase-shifter values of the BS hybrid analog precoder (near-field beamfocusing, beam squint), CSI-free at inference (p. 1, 3).
system: Downlink wideband THz UM-MIMO-OFDM; BS ULA with N=256 antennas, K=16 subarrays, single-antenna user; 300 GHz, 30 GHz bandwidth, 128 subcarriers; no RIS (p. 1, 4).
method: Unsupervised fully connected DNN (widths P, P/2, P/4, P/8, ReLU) trained offline with a hardware-aware Lagrangian loss, penalty ramp-up and progressive quantization blending (p. 3, 4).
data_channel: Own simulation: wideband near-field spherical-wave channel of eq. (3), user at rho~U[0,R], theta~U[0,pi]; 20,000 training samples; SNR drawn in [-15, 20] dB (p. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Trained over SNR -15 to 20 dB and random user positions; tested on the same channel model, sweeping SNR, angle, and distance (p. 4, 5).
baselines: Non-learned, perfect CSI: phase-delay focusing (PDF), heuristic (HB) and greedy (GB) beamfocusing, full-digital precoder; learned: reinforcement-learning (RL) beamfocusing [9], only in Fig. 3 (p. 4, 5).
metrics: Normalized array gain per subcarrier, average array gain per angle, spectral efficiency per subcarrier, and runtime per precoder design (p. 4, 5).
complexity: Inference complexity O(P^2); runtime 23.09 ms per design versus 242.84, 245.92, 690.96 ms for PDF, HB, GB with channel estimation, on a T4 GPU (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 4: "Training data are generated using the wideband near-field model in (3)"; a custom spherical-wave model, with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 4: "the MU location is uniformly distributed" over the range also used in tests (p. 5: "the MU distance is randomly distributed"); only SNR, angle, and distance sweeps, and transfer learning is future work (p. 5).
q3_support: p. 4: "and RL based scheme in [9]" is the earlier learned baseline, with PDF, HB, GB as non-learned ones; Fig. 3 compares array gain (p. 5: "the proposed DNN framework achieves higher performance").
q4_support: p. 5: "the proposed DNN framework has an inference complexity of" O(P^2), and Table I gives runtimes of 23.09 ms against 242.84 to 690.96 ms.
q5_support: p. 4: "Training data are generated using the wideband near-field model in (3)"; own simulation, with no code or data link and no public dataset or measurements.
notes: RL baseline [9] appears only in Fig. 3 (array gain), not in Fig. 4 or Table I (p. 5). Table I values were read from the page image. The user has one antenna but the BS has N=256, so the system check passes; RIS appears only in related work (p. 1). The paper does not say whether models were retrained for b=2 and b=3 phase-shifter bits (p. 4).
